questions.enonce_markdown:
Prayer is an essential element African Traditional Religion. How valid is this assertion?

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Prayer is communication with the divine. To say how valid the assertion is, one must describe the place of prayer in ATR and consider points that qualify it.

**1. Prayer in daily life.** Prayer is woven into everyday life. Families and individuals pray at rising, before meals, journeys, hunting or farming, and at birth, naming, marriage and death. It is usually spontaneous and spoken in the vernacular, rather than in a fixed form or at fixed times.

**2. To whom prayer is addressed.** Prayer is addressed to the Supreme Being, to the lesser divinities and spirits, and to the ancestors, often with the ancestors acting as intermediaries.

**3. Who prays.** Any person may pray, but family heads, elders, chiefs, priests and priestesses lead prayers for the household or community at shrines and in public rites.

**4. Types of prayer.** (i) Petition, for rain, health, children, success and protection. (ii) Thanksgiving, for harvest, recovery and safe return. (iii) Praise, calling on God by His names and attributes. (iv) Confession and appeasement, when a wrong has offended a spirit or ancestor. (v) Blessing and invocation, calling down protection on a new house, a marriage or a child.

**5. Accompanying acts.** Prayer is often joined to libations of water, palm wine or local drink, offerings, kola nuts, sacrifices, songs, dance and gestures, and it is a part of festivals and rites of passage.

**6. Prayer and community.** Communal prayer for rain or against epidemics builds unity and shows trust in God and the ancestors.

**7. Evidence that the assertion is valid.** Prayer expresses the believer's dependence on God and the spirits, and it occurs in almost all rituals. Proverbs, names and songs also contain prayers.

**8. Qualifications.** (i) In some societies the Supreme Being is seen as remote and approached mostly in crisis, while daily prayers go to divinities and ancestors. (ii) Sacrifice, ritual and divination sometimes receive more attention than words of prayer. (iii) Practices differ from one people to another and are passed on orally, so they are not uniform.

**Conclusion.** The assertion is largely valid: prayer is found in all areas of life and is one of the main ways in which Africans relate to God, the divinities and the ancestors, even though its forms and the beings addressed vary.
